links.reading: William, your steady attention can help George keep going when homework gets difficult. George, you may find it easier to stay with the task when William is nearby without taking over. Let him ask what kind of help you want, then stick to that. Behaviour check: At the kitchen table, agree whether William will help or simply sit nearby.

William, practical care can reassure George without asking him to explain every feeling. George, you may accept help more easily when it is offered plainly and leaves you some choice. Small acts can settle the morning rush, but do not assume either of you knows what the other needs. Behaviour check: Before school, ask whether help with one practical thing would be welcome.

George, your frustration can quickly stir William's worry, and William may step in before you are ready. William, your concern is real, but pressing for an answer can make George defend his privacy. Pause first, then offer a time to talk. Behaviour check: At bedtime, try one calm question and give George time to answer.

William, you may sense that George is upset before he says so. George, you may appreciate being understood without having to explain everything at once. But a guess can miss the mark, even when it comes from care. Ask rather than assume, and let George correct you. Behaviour check: After a difficult evening, ask George what would help instead of deciding for him.

William, you can make it easier for George to share what matters by showing interest without turning it into a test. George, you may respond well when William notices your effort and gives you space to enjoy it. A warm exchange can make the next hard conversation easier. Behaviour check: Ask George about something he enjoys, then listen without correcting.

William, your confidence in what George could do may lead you to ask for more than he can manage now. George, you may push back when encouragement sounds like a demand or a promise made for you. Let his present effort count before raising the bar. Behaviour check: When George says, “I've revised,” ask him to show what he knows.

William, George's different ideas can help you loosen a plan that no longer fits. George, you may find William more encouraging when you explain what you want to try. His support works best when it leaves room for your own choices. Behaviour check: This week, let George suggest one change to a shared plan and hear him out.

George, your strong reactions may draw William into helping quickly and generously. William, that care can steady him, but too much help may leave him feeling managed. Ask what he wants before adding advice or taking over. Behaviour check: When George is upset, ask whether he wants company, advice, or time alone.

William, your firm response can feel intense to George when he is protecting his privacy. George, a sharp answer may make William press harder, even when you want him to stop. Both of you can learn to pause before the disagreement grows. Behaviour check: After a door slam following a text, wait until calm before asking what upset George.

William, you may want to settle a disagreement quickly, while George may answer quickly to defend his choice. Neither of you has to win the first exchange. A pause can help George say what he needs and help William respond without escalating. Behaviour check: At bedtime, take a short break before returning to a disagreement.

William, your wish to reassure George may become a promise or explanation before he feels heard. George, you may need a quiet response more than a bigger plan. Keep support close to what he asked for, and check that you understood. Behaviour check: In the morning rush, ask George what would make the next step easier.

George, a sudden change of mind or plan may unsettle William when he is trying to offer steady support. William, insisting that things stay pleasant can make George feel he cannot be honest. Make room for a changed answer while keeping agreed limits clear. Behaviour check: When a plan changes, ask what changed before deciding what to do.
